messages:
alex: Heads-up: stg gRPC streaming RPCs are getting cut after ~90-140s when routed through edge ALB -> NAT gateway. No server-side close in logs. Anyone else seeing this?

maya: yep, noticed on inference-stg earlier. Client shows `HTTP/2 stream closed by peer` then gRPC status=14 intermittently.

chris: could be ALB idle timeout, TCP keepalive, or NAT/conntrack churn. ALB default is 60s but we moved to 120 for most groups. Timing sounds like conntrack though.

linh: on eu we hit similar with ephemeral port exhaustion during bursty streams. Conntrack entries spiked and NAT started sending RSTs.

deploy-bot: Deploy started 1900456700 -> rolling 10% traffic to stg-new-edge :rocket:

maya: I grabbed a tcpdump at the edge and see RSTs originating from the NAT GW right after a server chunk. snippet: 

```
# tcpdump -n -s0 -w - | tshark -r - -Y "tcp && tcp.flags.reset==1" -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e tcp.srcport -e ip.dst -e tcp.dstport
10:12:34.567 10.0.3.2:35012 -> 10.20.1.5:443 RST
10:12:34.571 10.0.3.2:35012 -> 10.20.1.5:443 RST
```

sam: can you paste `conntrack -S` and `ss -tnp` counts? also check `nf_conntrack_max` and current usage.

alex: conntrack table shows ~250k entries, nf_conntrack_max=262144, nearing limit during the spike. `ss -tn` shows many TIME_WAIT/ESTABLISHED to the same port ranges.

linh: that explains it — when the table hits capacity the kernel starts dropping/misrouting tuples which looks like RST to endpoints. Fixes we've used: increase `nf_conntrack_max`, tune `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established`, and add more NAT capacity (more NAT instances or larger NAT gateway). Also consider source port randomization and setting `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` wider.

chris: short-term mitigations: 1) increase conntrack and timeouts 2) scale NAT pool 3) enable gRPC keepalive pings from client to keep flows active 4) set ALB/edge proxy idle timeout to 0s or very high if safe. For Envoy we use `idle_timeout: 0s` on upstream clusters to avoid proxy-initiated drain.

maya: tried `grpc.keepalive_time_ms=60000` on client but still saw cuts — probably NAT reusing mapping before keepalive kicks or asymmetric path.

ops-bot: Observability note: added alert `nat_conntrack_usage > 80%` to stg for 10m.

sam: another angle — if ALB is terminating HTTP/2 and re-establishing to backend (HTTP/1), that can create half-closed behavior. Confirm end-to-end h2 passthrough.

alex: confirmed ALB->edge-proxy preserves HTTP/2 in this path, but some older fronting proxies downgrade in fallback. Not the main path here.

linh: runbook snippet I'm going to paste for quick remediate: 
```
# runbook snippet
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=86400
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="10240 60999"
# scale NAT instances / upgrade NAT gateway SKU
```

alex: plan: 1) immediate bump conntrack on stg NAT hosts, 2) scale NAT gateway pool + enable more egress capacity for this test path, 3) roll traffic to new path (rolling 50% in next 30m) with metrics on stream success/failure and conntrack. I'll post results here.

maya: thx — will watch gRPC error rate and stream durations. please include pcap and conntrack dumps in the ticket. :+1:

chris: if this persists after capacity bump, we'll try temporary tcp-mode target group to avoid ALB HTTP/2 edge behavior and see if that stabilizes streams.

alex: copying @maria for visibility on cost impact if we scale NAT. Also noting this could hit prod if traffic pattern shifts similarly.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-453 (stg gRPC stream truncation)

alex: I'll update ticket with timeline and playbook entries when done. Appreciated everyone for quick triage.
